sacubitril‐valsartan and its active ingredient sacubitril improve the cardiac function in a rodent model of chronic myocardial infarct by downregulation of exosomal miR‐ 181a and attenuation of myocardial hypertrophy and fibrosis.

the role of miR‐182a in cardiac function in a rodent model of chronic myocardial injury.
a new potential mechanism for sacubitril‐based therapy in the treatment of chronic myocardial injury.
the identification and characterization of the exosomal miRNA‐mediated mechanism of sacubitrile/valsartan‐induced pleiotropic effects in the rodent myocardial infarct model.

sacubitril‐valsartan may have a therapeutic potential to attenuate myocardial fibrosis by the downregulation in exosomal miR‐ 181a.

exosome‐mediated miR‐181‐5p downregulation is involved in the beneficial effects of sacubtiril/valsartans in the treatment of myocardial fibrotic injury.

the modulation of the exosome miRNA content may represent a novel therapeutic strategy in cardiovascular disease.
